sentences.claim: "This systematic process of identifying the objective and planning a course to obtain it applies to all areas and levels of preparations"
CAIB says "schedule deadlines are an important management tool"
DOE recommends that you "Establish metrics to measure program performance and evaluate the effectiveness of actions implemented from lessons learned"
The accounting textbook defines a performance measurement system as one that "evaluates management in a way that will link the goals of the corporation with those of the manager"
Warfighting splits every mission into the task and the intent, and says "Of the two, the intent is predominant"
It adds that a changing situation may make the task obsolete while the intent continues to guide action
It also says a subordinate "who is not given a clear purpose for the assigned mission should ask for one"
The textbook change process builds a "guiding coalition" of influential people who act as ambassadors
Warfighting says subordinates "inform the commander of what they have done, but they do not wait for permission"
It also says "The senior intervenes in a subordinate's execution only by exception"
DOE's own change guidance says only "Consider a Steering Committee," calling it "a temporary organization established in an advisory capacity"
CAIB says that as information moves up a hierarchy, "weak signals drop from memos, problem identification systems, and formal presentations"
It also says "the same conclusions, repeated over time, can result in problems eventually being deemed non-problems"
In its words, "Little by little, NASA was accepting more and more risk in order to stay on schedule"
The Rogers Commission criticised NASA for requiring "a contractor to prove that it was not safe to launch, rather than proving it was safe"
It says "people cannot perform better than the organization supporting them"
It describes a just culture in which "people who make honest errors and mistakes are not blamed"
The wildfire guide says that, for many in the fire community, "'accountability' had become synonymous with 'punitive actions'"
Its learning reviews now carry an assurance of "no punitive actions"
The textbook opens change by trying to "establish a sense of urgency" and to "create a burning platform"
It also found that dangerous aspects of the 1986 culture "remained unchanged"
DOE describes its approach as "not so much a program as it is a distinct way of thinking"
It notes that "most daily management activity involves some degree of change"
It says "Competence does not guarantee positive control"

DOE says people in highly reliable organisations "practice error-prevention rigorously, regardless of their perception of a task's risk and simplicity, how routine it is, and how competent the performer"
Warfighting calls doctrine "authoritative" but "not prescriptive"
It says method should be prescribed "only to the degree that is essential for coordination"
In the same passage it also calls for "new structuring, rules, and management training" (list item under 'CAIB holds both positions at once')
sentences.missing: The phrase is there, but CAIB wants the new structuring and rules 'to restore deference to technical experts, empower engineers ... and allow safety concerns to be freely aired'. That is the flexibility side, not an opposing pro-procedure position. The text also sits in a separate column-paragraph, so 'same passage' is doubtful.

sentences.claim: It contrasts the submarine programme's rigour with NASA's, saying "NASA requirements are clearly documented but are also more easily waived"
DOE ties its practices to "line management responsibility for safety"
It faults the Shuttle Program for controlling both engineering and safety
Warfighting has seniors intervene only by exception
DOE puts its emphasis on the individual keeping control and resisting overconfidence
sentences.missing: DOE does warn about overconfidence and personal dependencies. Nothing supports that this is its overall emphasis: the handbook says error stems from 'incompatible management and leadership practices and organizational weaknesses' and that 'people cannot perform better than the organization supporting them'.

sentences.claim: It moves toward understanding "a network of influences, or performance shaping factors"
The wildfire learning review develops lessons "without recommendations"
sentences.missing: The guide says the FLA develops lessons 'without recommendations', but its Learning Review is defined by having recommendations as an output (focus groups, a Learning Review Board, a Safety Action Plan). The claim as worded attributes 'without recommendations' to the learning review and drops that the guide allows recommendations.

sentences.claim: Warfighting says "we cannot allow decentralized initiative without some means of providing unity, or focus, to the various efforts"
It names a main effort: "This is how I will achieve a decision; everything else is secondary"
DOE's suggestions to "Designate a devil's advocate" and call "timeouts" are cheap to adopt
sentences.missing: Both suggestions are in DOE as team practices (problem-solving, shared understanding of status). The judgement that they are 'cheap to adopt', and their use as a weak-signal channel past a KPI roll-up, are in no source.

sentences.claim: DOE lists ignoring operating experience from "other industries" as an at-risk practice

note: Only sentences that carry a marker are graded. Unmarked lead-ins (e.g. 'CAIB holds both positions at once', 'CAIB found that after Challenger, ...', 'CAIB issues recommendations') are not; all their quotations were checked and are in CAIB, apart from the framing noted at n=28. n=15 names the Rogers Commission while citing CAIB; CAIB quotes the Commission's finding, so it is not counted as wrong_book.
